correctness.rationale: The Rota–Baxter identity gives scalar functional zero, scalar part of P(1) zero, B squared zero, and 2Bv=0; conversely these equations make both sides vanish for every pair of elements. Cubic nilpotency and the sharp characteristic-two example follow directly. The centralizer in GL(V) acts transitively on four explicit vector strata, with the last restricted to characteristic two. Rank-r square-zero matrix counts follow by image/kernel/isomorphism choices. A uniform Gaussian-product estimate and rank concentration establish the finite-field asymptotic. Direct exhaustive finite-field identities and full orbit partitions in verify.py agree; finite cases do not prove asymptotics.

originality.rationale: Farooq, arXiv:2605.15670v1, gives the exact same algebra in characteristic zero with P squared zero; it does not treat characteristic two. The new operator phenomenon is the precise positive-characteristic obstruction 2Bv=0 and its cubic nilpotency, sharp minimal dimension, exact finite-field distribution and fixed-field genericity. The abstract conjugacy orbit parametrization is a standard square-zero restriction of the enhanced nilpotent cone, explicitly credited to Achar–Henderson and Bellamy–Boos, and is not itself claimed original. The accessible searched sources did not show this characteristic-two Rota–Baxter statement or generic index-three law, while historical-priority uncertainty remains.
residual_risks: A historically earlier positive-characteristic treatment of this exact first-order-neighborhood algebra could exist under another name and entail some or all conclusions.
Enhanced-nilpotent orbit theory fully covers the abstract marked-square-zero orbit stratum, so novelty cannot rest on that part alone.
Full texts of Achar–Henderson and Bellamy–Boos were not materially inspected; abstract-level assessment cannot exclude hidden Rota–Baxter applications.

value.rationale: For a natural algebra already motivating a 2026 complete characteristic-zero classification, the exact characteristic-two obstruction changes the maximum operator nilpotency index from two to three; the boundary is attained in the smallest three-dimensional algebra. The theorem calculates full finite-field operator counts and shows index three becomes overwhelmingly common at fixed even field order. It provides a complete field-sensitive operator picture rather than an arbitrary isolated count. Abstract marked-nilpotent orbit methods are prior, not inflated as independent contributions.
